The original #2151/#2542 approved fixture/read-authority class remains open.

## Concepts, owners and exhaustive consumption

This batch removes incidental raw SQL/fixture authority from the enumerated
twenty physical-read helpers and their complete typed caller set, plus the
six-domain channel budget failure scanner. It does not change production
admission, mutation, lifecycle or error policy. Governing platform-spec.yaml
entries are channel_budget_notice_storage_observation and
selected_served_physical_read_roles, alongside the existing selected-store
inspection and closed executable-delivery ownership contracts.

The canonical selected lifetime is the ORIGINAL ReceiverStateReader and its
InspectSnapshot context. The fixture neither constructs nor closes a selected
adapter/coordinator. Scalar absence is restored only after successful cleanup;
cancellation/cleanup errors publish no value. Detached diagnostic projections
preserve query errors, prefix rows, column/scan/iteration failures, and the
caller's original fatal versus logging behavior. They are not an empty-success
fallback. Reporter helpers consume the actual Endpoint plus inspection role,
not a renamed whole raw fixture. Dev scratch captures the actual inspection
reader from the same original production projection hook.

## Closure limits and feedback

Closure is the finite helper/caller/diagnostic observation subset, not the parent
failure class. The broader debt tail is the actual ratchet result. Existing
event-count, Template9 workflow-state, deployment, M01/Docker and fork-deadline
qualification holds remain unwaived except the explicitly superseded B-specific
fork prerequisite. The inherited fork residual remains tracked in #2535 under
ordinary qualification policy. No new issue/watchlist is needed; architecture
feedback stays in #2542 under the existing selected-authority node. The smell is
incidental whole-fixture arguments spreading raw read authority. Existing
domain-owned projections plus the original inspection lifetime are the better
direction, not another generic read framework or compatibility seam. Expected
ROI is reduced fixture-maintenance fan-out, not a claim of faster runtime/tests.
